record.name: Ukraine
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A draft EU-aligned AI law would create a digital regulator that sets rules, with checks and post-market monitoring of general-purpose models, but it is still being drafted.

related_bodies.name: Planned Digital Regulator (draft AI law)
related_bodies.role: It would write by-laws and guidance, with checks and post-market monitoring of general-purpose models; the draft law is not yet adopted.

next_check.reason: Draft AI law is planned for development during 2026.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English results include the national LLM's benchmarking and safety work and a government account of UK AI Security Institute red-teaming for Diia.AI. Testing Ukraine's own model or application, and work by the UK institute, do not establish a Ukrainian national AISI. The existing parliamentary digital-regulator proposal remains rule-setting and oversight; no newly retrieved qualifying designation was found. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Parliament's 2026 account sets out proposed digital-regulator powers. The Dnistrianskyi Center's separately authored advocacy article of 18 July 2024 proposes a Ukrainian AI safety institute. That older source is historical context, not a current official denial; its statement about plans applies to 2024. The two retrieved texts have distinct authors and origins.
check.governance_note: The parliamentary account describes proposed digital-regulator powers and AI market supervision. A separate historical advocacy statement is not an official current absence finding.

record.notes: The Dnistrianskyi Center advocacy article was published on 18 July 2024. Its statement that no corresponding institute was planned describes the position at that time, not a current official finding. The 2026 parliamentary account separately describes proposed digital-regulator powers.
